scope: Theorem 9.3 (Uniform two-mark bound) of the manuscript “Radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws for honeycomb walks” (preprints/Radial-transfer-estimates-and-polygon-length-laws-for-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 02d2e8df0dcf370b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 77. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix C0 ≥ 1. Consider a sequence of the even site arrays defining H in (9.1), with the two allowed shifts of Section 9.4. Both marked sites have the same shift. Suppose that |L| + 1 = k → ∞, 3k ≤ N ≤ kC0 , N even. Here L denotes the shorter site block; the radial period below will be denoted P. Let ai, di count the unshifted and shifted color sites, omitting the two marks, in sector i, with sector 1 equal to R and sector 2 equal to L. Assume a1 ≍ N, a2 ≍ k, a1 ≥ a2, inf 0≤ρ≤1 max i=1,2 |di/ai − ρ| −→ 0. The comparison constants are fixed along the sequence. Then |H | ≤ k−4/3+o(1) . (9.19) Thus, for every fixed ε > 0, the scalar is at most k−4/3+ε for all sufficiently large members of the sequence, after absorbing a fixed multiplicative constant into the exponent loss.
